correctness.rationale: For any finite abelian alphabet with a symmetric perfect bicharacter, the one-coordinate Schur complement of the full Fourier table has inverse \(q^{-1}\overline{b(a,c)}\). Zeta factorization on partial nonzero assignments gives \(H=ZDZ^{T}\), with invertible block tensors and Boolean-interval Möbius inverse. Summing the exact blocks yields (1) with the correct sign and union cutoff. Counting support unions gives exact (3). The apex diagonal is the degree-r binomial sum \(S_{n,r}\) with leading term \((-1)^r((q-1)/q)^r n^r/r!\); all other Frobenius terms are lower by \(n^{-1}\), proving \(\|H^{-1}\|_2\) sharply. Intersection counting proves \(\|H\|_2\sim|B_{n,r}|\), and rank-one perturbation gives the stated singular-vector localization. Exact two-sided checks for q=2 and the two q=4 groups, plus six numerical and Frobenius checks (including q=6), corroborate but do not replace the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Bounded searches of published records, accessible cumulative claims, and directly relevant primary literature found neither a uniform support-union inverse kernel on every group Hamming ball nor the associated universal sharp \(n^{2r}\) condition-number constant. The closest tensor Fourier rank-defect theorem addresses a different optimization; Hamming MacWilliams duality addresses entire weight partitions, not principal inverses. A previously reported complete q=2, r=2 spectrum yields only one special asymptotic instance; it does not dominate the general result. Priority risk remains for unlocated zeta-compressed Fourier inversion identities.
residual_risks: A broader established Möbius inversion or poset Fourier compression theorem could already imply (1); priority is not certified.

value.rationale: Square Fourier interpolation on low-Hamming-weight words is natural in low-interaction Fourier analysis and finite sampling. The theorem provides a nontrivial complete inverse kernel, an exact geometric zero pattern, a finite exact Frobenius formula, and a sharp noise-amplification constant for all fixed radii and every finite abelian alphabet, independent of group isomorphism type. Singular-vector localization identifies the precise asymptotically worst-conditioned sample. This infinite-radius family and universality are materially beyond a one-radius numerical census or elementary invertibility statement. It does not claim finite-size exact singular spectra or growing-radius uniformity.
